messages.content:
You review lifestyle plans written by FOXO's lifestyle coach for a member in India.

You will see the member's profile, the abnormal results the plan targets, and the full plan. Judge whether a member could act on the plan tomorrow. Do not judge medical correctness here; other checks cover that.

For each criterion, first write one or two sentences of reasoning, then set passed to true or false.

Criteria (use these ids exactly, one entry each):
- specific: Recommendations give concrete foods with portions or timing, not generic advice like "eat healthy".
- practical: The foods are everyday Indian foods a member could easily buy and cook.
- explained: Each recommendation says how it helps the linked biomarker.
- activity_concrete: The activity advice says what to do, for how long and how often.

Respond with a single JSON object that matches this JSON schema:
{"$defs": {"CriterionVerdict": {"properties": {"criterion": {"title": "Criterion", "type": "string"}, "reasoning": {"title": "Reasoning", "type": "string"}, "passed": {"title": "Passed", "type": "boolean"}}, "required": ["criterion", "reasoning", "passed"], "title": "CriterionVerdict", "type": "object"}}, "properties": {"criteria": {"items": {"$ref": "#/$defs/CriterionVerdict"}, "title": "Criteria", "type": "array"}}, "required": ["criteria"], "title": "JudgeOutput", "type": "object"}

Diet: non_vegetarian. Allergies: none. Conditions: none.
Abnormal results: ldl 205.0 mg/dL (high), triglycerides 310.0 mg/dL (high)

Plan:
Focus areas: LDL cholesterol; Triglycerides; Heart-healthy Indian meals; Gentle activity only as advised by doctor
Foods to eat:
- Breakfast within 1 hour of waking: 40 g dry oats cooked in water or skimmed milk with 1 small guava or apple, 5 days a week; on other days have 2 ragi idlis with 1 katori sambar. (why: Oats and ragi provide soluble fibre that helps lower LDL cholesterol; whole fruit adds fibre without sweetened drinks.; linked to ldl)
- Lunch before 2 pm: 1 cup cooked bajra, jowar or ragi (or brown rice) with 1 katori dal, 2 katoris seasonal sabzi and 1 bowl salad. (why: Whole millets and dal give fibre and slowly digested carbohydrates, helping lower triglycerides when they replace refined grains.; linked to triglycerides)
- Mid-morning or evening snack: 1 small katori (about 30 g) sprouted moong or chana salad, or roasted chana, instead of biscuits or fried snacks. (why: Sprouts and chana are high-fibre protein foods that improve fullness and support lower LDL cholesterol.; linked to ldl)
- Dinner before 8 pm: 1 katori dal or rajma/chana 3-4 days a week with 1-2 phulka without ghee and 2 katoris cooked vegetables; include grilled or baked fish 100-150 g 2 times a week instead of fried or fatty meat. (why: High-fibre legumes and fish in place of fried or fatty meats help lower triglycerides and support heart health.; linked to triglycerides)
- Cook with a measured total of 3 teaspoons (15 ml) oil per day for your portion; use mustard, groundnut or rice bran oil and do not reuse deep-frying oil. (why: Limiting added oil reduces excess calories and helps reduce triglycerides.; linked to triglycerides)
Foods to limit or avoid: Deep-fried foods such as samosa, pakora, puri and fried chicken; Sweets, jaggery, honey, sugary drinks, fruit juices and bakery items; Refined flour (maida) products such as white bread, naan, biscuits and cakes; Processed and fatty meats such as sausage, salami, bacon and fatty red meat; Butter, ghee, cream and full-fat dairy in large amounts; Reusing deep-frying oil
Activity: Follow your doctor's advice strictly: avoid strenuous exercise pending cardiology review. Do only gentle activity, such as a 15-20 minute easy walk at a comfortable pace after meals, 5 days a week if your doctor agrees. Stop immediately if you feel chest pain, breathlessness, dizziness or unusual tiredness.
Sleep: Aim for 7-8 hours of sleep nightly. Keep a regular sleep schedule, avoid screens 1 hour before bed, and finish dinner at least 2-3 hours before lying down.
Retest in 12 weeks

response: {"criteria": [{"criterion": "specific", "reasoning": "Every recommendation names exact foods with portions and timing: 40 g dry oats, 2 ragi idlis, 1 cup cooked millet, 30 g sprouts, 100-150 g fish, 3 teaspoons oil, plus meal windows (breakfast within 1 hour of waking, lunch before 2 pm, dinner before 8 pm). Nothing is generic.", "passed": true}, {"criterion": "practical", "reasoning": "Oats, guava, ragi idlis, sambar, bajra/jowar, dal, sabzi, sprouted moong, chana, phulka, rajma, mustard/groundnut oil and fish are all everyday Indian foods that are inexpensive and easy to buy and cook anywhere in India.", "passed": true}, {"criterion": "explained", "reasoning": "Each food recommendation includes a 'why' statement with the mechanism tied to the linked biomarker, e.g. soluble fibre in oats/ragi lowering LDL, whole millets replacing refined grains to lower triglycerides, and limiting oil to reduce triglycerides.", "passed": true}, {"criterion": "activity_concrete", "reasoning": "The activity advice specifies what to do (easy walk at a comfortable pace after meals), for how long (15-20 minutes), and how often (5 days a week), while appropriately gating it on the doctor's cardiology review and listing clear stop symptoms.", "passed": true}]}
